sentences.text: Joost Farwerck, born in 1965, joined KPN in 1994 after graduating in Law from the University of Amsterdam and has over 31 years of experience at the company and in the telecom and technology industry; he was appointed CEO and Chairman of the Board of Management of Koninklijke KPN N.V. on December 1, 2019.

Earlier KPN roles included Manager Sales and Corporate Secretary to the Board and Supervisory Board, Senior EVP Consumer Residential in 2011, and Managing Director Netherlands from 2012, with responsibility for KPN's Dutch activities.

sentences.quote: currently interim Chairman of the Board of Management, has been a member of the Board of Management since 2013 and is currently Chief Operating Officer (COO), a role he has fulfilled since 2014
sentences.text: He joined the Board of Management in 2013 and served as Chief Operating Officer from 2014, acting as interim Chairman before his CEO appointment.

sentences.quote:
As CEO, he is responsible for the overall strategy and performance of KPN. His main task is to set strategic

sentences.text: As CEO he is responsible for KPN's overall strategy and performance, setting strategic priorities with emphasis on sustainability, innovation, cybersecurity and diversity.

sentences.quote: Together with Glaspoort, our joint venture, we remain clear leader in the Dutch fiber market.
sentences.text: KPN leads the Dutch fiber market, together with its Glaspoort joint venture, and is shifting from building coverage to activating customers, with fiber now 72% of its retail broadband base.

sentences.quote: these priorities support our ambition to grow service revenues and EBITDA by approximately 3% and free cash flow by approximately 7% on average over the full strategic period
sentences.text: Its Connect, Activate and Grow strategy rests on investing in leading networks, growing and protecting the customer base, and simplifying the operating model, targeting about 3% average growth in service revenues and EBITDA and about 7% in free cash flow over the strategic period.
After the heavy fiber build, KPN expects a Capex step-down of roughly EUR 250m in 2027 to below EUR 1bn, lifting operating free cash flow about 10% a year on average.
KPN intends a regular dividend of EUR 0.20 per share over 2026 and completed a EUR 250m buyback in May 2026, with a cumulative buyback target of up to EUR 1bn over 2024-2027.
Returns are solid, with ROCE of 14.4%, a 15% ambition for 2027, and leverage at 2.5 times.

thesis_pillars.text: KPN leads the Dutch fiber market, together with its Glaspoort joint venture, and is shifting from building coverage to activating customers, with fiber now 72% of its retail broadband base. Its Connect, Activate and Grow strategy rests on investing in leading networks, growing and protecting the customer base, and simplifying the operating model, targeting about 3% average growth in service revenues and EBITDA and about 7% in free cash flow over the strategic period.
